name: _sparse_mm_reduce_impl
description: Representative ATen signature, copied verbatim (not exclusive): aten::_sparse_mm_reduce_impl(Tensor self, Tensor other, str reduce) -> (Tensor, Tensor). This one overload is only the representative contract; the original Gems pytest owns the full contract for overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and tests must never be removed or the reference behavior adapted to fit this signature. All supplied registered schemas: aten::_sparse_mm_reduce_impl(Tensor self, Tensor other, str reduce) -> (Tensor, Tensor). Semantics evidenced by the tests: self is a non-hybrid 2-D sparse-CSR tensor of shape (M, K) and other is a 2-D strided dense tensor of shape (K, N) whose dtype matches self.values() and whose size(0) equals self.size(1); reduce is a case-sensitive string whose exercised modes are "sum", "mean", "amax" and "amin", and the tested unsupported strings ("prod", the unknown string "bogus", the empty string and upper-case "SUM") each raise RuntimeError. The call computes the sparse-dense product reduced per output entry and returns two tensors in one tuple: out, the dense (M, N) result, and arg_out, the argument-index tensor. Outside grad mode arg_out is an empty tensor in the CSR crow_indices dtype; in grad mode amax/amin fill arg_out with the winning row index per output entry while sum/mean keep it empty, so arg_out behavior is grad-mode/state dependent rather than expressed by this model. The tested CPU kernel accepts value dtypes float32, float16, bfloat16 and float64; the test list appends bfloat16 and float64 only when the shared static device flags report them, which is a test-helper gating (tu.make_input allocates on flag_gems.device), not a kernel restriction. int8, uint8, int32, int64, bool and float8 raise RuntimeError. Other native-invalid forms raise RuntimeError: dense or COO self, hybrid CSR self with dense_dim() > 0, 3-D other, other dtype mismatch, and other.size(0) != self.size(1).
